R355.note: Both values bound via SqlParameter; null-coalescing to empty string reproduces the original concatenation semantics, and an invalid date now fails at conversion rather than widening the predicate.

R356.note: Adds the same can:update,order policy gate the sibling mutating routes use, which is the authorization the finding calls for.

R357.note:
redis-py bulk-string encoding closes the CRLF/space split, but the return value silently changes from the raw b'+OK
' bytes to True and the write-up does not say so.

R358.note: random_bytes(32) hex token is the right CSPRNG; the token format change to 64 hex chars is stated plainly (a reset_token column narrower than 64 chars would be a follow-up).

R359.note: Tika magic detection plus server-generated name closes the header trust and fits the contract, but the added ImageIO re-encode lossily recompresses, strips EXIF orientation and turns a valid CMYK/unsupported JPEG into a 500 via the thrown IOException, consequences the write-up does not state.

R360.note: Identifier allowlist is the correct shape for a FROM-clause name and the contract calls for the restriction; note the two extra table names are invented rather than taken from the case.

R361.note: Enyim key validation rejects space/control chars so the inline command cannot be split, but the constructor now takes IMemcachedClient instead of Socket and values are written through DefaultTranscoder with non-zero flags, a wire-format change other readers would see that the write-up does not state (its RESP/length-prefix claim is also inaccurate for the default text protocol).

R362.note: Removing the shell exec closes the vector for a command whose only purpose was echo, but the response body loses the Utils.printOSCommandResults HTML wrapper while the write-up asserts the same result.

R363.note: html/template contextual escaping with the same markup; output for benign input is unchanged.

R364.note: Length checked against payload.size() before the copy; oversized input is rejected by exception, which the contract permits, and length always matches bytes written.

R365.note: Null check precedes strcmp via short-circuit; unset variable yields the disabled result the contract asks for.

R366.note: Restricting the array to RS256 removes the public-key-as-HMAC confusion; HS256 tokens never verified legitimately under the original (wrong key), and the now-unused hmacSecret is stated.

R367.note: realpath containment with separator-suffixed prefix check closes traversal; header now uses basename of the validated path and is set after validation, both visible in the write-up, with 404 semantics preserved.

R368.note: allowed_classes=false disables object construction while keeping the native format, so legacy rows still load; the contract's JSON-written rows are not addressed but the fix makes no format change and does not regress them relative to the original.

R369.note: filterArgs overload escapes the value per RFC 2254; new SearchControls() is exactly what null meant, so scope and attribute return are unchanged.

R370.note: th:text fully closes the utext sink, but a rich-text body now displays its tags as literal text instead of being allowlist-sanitized as the contract calls for; the write-up states the assumption and the sanitizer alternative, so stated rather than silent.
